item.title: Reading the Wind
item.description: The proverb isogaba maware was born on Lake Biwa: when the wind is bad, the long bridge at Seta beats the fast boat from Yabase. On choosing research topics, reading currents, and the people who walk toward Seta while the lake is still quiet.

item.title: Profile
item.description:
My work explores how AI can turn scientific knowledge into real-world impact. I believe we can design more intelligent systems for innovation.

I now carry this work into the wild as an Impact Fellow at the Northwestern Innovation Institute, Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University.

Publications

  • Asymmetric returns to basic-applied career shifts. N. Higashide, K. Nishimoto, K. Asatani and I. Sakata. Quantitative Science Studies (2026).
  • Mid-career pitfall of consecutive success in science. N. Higashide, T. Miura, Y. Tomokiyo, K. Asatani and I. Sakata. Scientific Reports 14, 28172 (2024).
  • Quantifying advances from basic research to applied research in material science. N. Higashide, Y. Zhang, K. Asatani, T. Miura and I. Sakata. Technovation 135, 103050 (2023).
  • Cold exciton electroluminescence from air-suspended carbon nanotube split-gate devices. N. Higashide, M. Yoshida, T. Uda, A. Ishii and Y. K. Kato. Applied Physics Letters 110, 191101 (2017).
